facts.text: Ollama web search is a hosted API feature that returns search results or fetched page content for applications that need current information. It is separate from local model inference and requires an Ollama account API key.

Fetch a single page when the application needs page content. $ curl https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"url":"https://docs.ollama.com/"}' {"title":"Ollama documentation","content":"##### snipped #####","links":[##### snipped #####]}

A community Reddit report says a 401 on web search, seen when building Ollama from source, went away once the OLLAMA_API_KEY environment variable took precedence over the SSH-key signing path. This is a single unverified report.

Local-only mode: set `disable_ollama_cloud: true` in ~/.ollama/server.json or export OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1, then restart. This disables Ollama cloud models and web search, and the logs show `Ollama cloud disabled: true`.

The official FAQ lets operators run local-only by setting OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1 or `disable_ollama_cloud: true` in ~/.ollama/server.json, which removes cloud models and web search and logs 'Ollama cloud disabled: true'.
Ollama can run in local only mode by disabling Ollama's cloud features. By turning off Ollama's cloud features, you will lose the ability to use Ollama's cloud models and web search.

The official docs list no numeric rate limits, quotas, HTTP error codes or content size limits for web_search/web_fetch. Third-party aggregator pages claim cloud limits are tier-based concurrency (Free 1, Pro 3, Max 10 cloud models) and 5-hour/7-day usage windows, but these concern cloud model inference, not necessarily the search endpoints.

Because the endpoints are hosted on ollama.com, any host calling them needs outbound internet access and an account key. Search query text and fetched URLs leave the local network, so air-gapped or egress-restricted deployments cannot use them.

The search endpoint runs at https://ollama.com/api/web_search and accepts a query plus an optional result limit. Treat returned snippets as retrieval context that still needs citation, filtering, or summarization in the application layer.

Verify hosted web search returns results with a bearer token. $ curl https://ollama.com/api/web_search \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"query":"what is ollama?","max_results":3}' {"results":[{"title":"Ollama","url":"https://ollama.com/","content":"Cloud models are now available..."}]}

Keep result count small for prompt injection review. $ curl https://ollama.com/api/web_search -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" -d '{"query":"site:docs.ollama.com embeddings","max_results":2}' {"results":[##### snipped #####]}

Search and fetch results can be thousands of tokens. Ollama recommends raising the model context length to at least ~32000 tokens, and says its cloud models run at full context length. The official example agent uses qwen3:4b with think=True and truncates each tool output to 2000*4 characters.

web_search is POST https://ollama.com/api/web_search with required string `query` and optional integer `max_results` (default 5, max 10). The response is an object whose `results` array holds items with `title`, `url` and `content` (a snippet).

Both endpoints are hosted on ollama.com, not on a local Ollama server, and need an API key created at ollama.com/settings/keys from a free account. The key goes in the OLLAMA_API_KEY environment variable or an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
curl https://ollama.com/api/web_search \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "query": "what is ollama?" }'
curl --request POST \ --url https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $OLLAMA_API_KEY" \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "url": "ollama.com" }'
web_fetch is POST https://ollama.com/api/web_fetch with required string `url`. The response has `title`, `content` (main page content) and `links` (links found on the page).

Ollama ships a Python MCP server (web-search-mcp.py in the ollama-python repo) that exposes web search to any MCP client. Docs show config for Cline and Codex (command uv, with OLLAMA_API_KEY in env). Goose is shown only in screenshots.
Choose a [cloud model](https://ollama.com/search?c=cloud). The cloud API does not support stateful Responses, built-in web search through `/v1/responses`, or custom/freeform tool-call replay.
Codex web-search requests sent through the Ollama profile are executed by Ollama for both local and cloud models. Sign in with `ollama signin` to use the web-search service.
Web search is enabled automatically. It requires access to Ollama's cloud and a model that supports tools. Run `ollama signin` if needed.
<Note>Ollama web search for local models requires `ollama signin`.</Note>
Web search and fetch were announced 2025-09-24. The announcement calls the free tier generous for individuals and says higher rate limits come with Ollama's cloud subscription. It gives no numbers.

Returned snippets are untrusted retrieval context, so the application must handle citation, filtering and prompt-injection review. One third-party guide advises keeping max_results small to make that review tractable, and a task-scoped key that is rotated after testing and never stored in a repo.

The Python library (`ollama>=0.6.0`) exposes `ollama.web_search(query)` and `ollama.web_fetch(url)`, the latter returning a WebFetchResponse. The JavaScript library (`ollama@>=0.6.0`) exposes `client.webSearch()` and `client.webFetch()`. Both SDKs can pass the functions as tools to chat().

The official example agent loop is `while True` with no iteration cap and no exception handling, and it passes model-supplied arguments straight to the tool. A production agent needs a loop cap, argument validation and try/except around tool calls.
